questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The selection of courses at the University and the nature in Canada

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is hard to be completely objective on the overall experience, because I had to end my exchange earlier than planned because of illness.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: fairly easy, although there is a lot of information, and it was sometimes hard to know who to ask for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had some information meetings, and got some assistance regarding our living situation - but a kind of contact person would have been helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I missed a little bit of understanding regarding how overwhelming it can be to travel to a new country and start at a new university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I just applied for the ones there were, and hoped to get something - I don't really remember the different options, I had just heard that it was hard and expensive to find a place to stay in Vancouver, so I just hoped to get any kind of on campus facility.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Where I stayed we had a big kitchen, but there were no kinds of kitchen remedies, such as pans, glasses or anything like that. There was a microwave and dishwasher though.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That we were able to move in only one day prior to class start, as I recall. And the kitchen is empty, so you have to be quick to go to a second hand store or something like that to get remedies for the kitchen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it really strange that there weren't invested in kitchen remedies, because everyone bought stuff that had to be emptied again when the term ended. My friend also had a mouse in the house at some point.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think the hard part was the mix of having to register at the host university and also having to be in contact with KU about the registration, and 'forhåndsgodkendelse' and stuff like that. And also having to find out which classes were available to you - some classes you could only take on term 1 and I was there on term 2.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know - I don't think I got any help, but there was probably an email somewhere you could write to for help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I had to change it once, because I had applied for some classes I couldn't get.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about it, it was still a possibility to change classes after arrival - although you might have to be in contact with KU about that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really exciting classes - but pretty different from KU. A lot more activity required, not as much theory as I was used to, which was kind of hard to get used to.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three 200 level courses and one 100 level course - which is 2nd and 1st year level - It was actually a bit hard to go 'down' in levels, as I was a third year student - I felt like they demanded more than they actually did. I could only take 100 and 200 level courses because I took classes from different academic fields.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more interaction with the prof. - they demanded more of you, but a lot more help and private interaction was also available.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANTH 206 - Witches, Vampires and Zombies: Anthropology of the Supernatural
ANTH 213 - Sex, Gender, and Culture
CRWR 206 - Introduction to Writing for the Screen
GRSJ 101 - Introduction to Social Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Witches, Vampires and Zombies, to anyone who thinks anthropology sounds interesting, and who would find it fun or interesting to learn about the supernatural - I learned a lot about anthropology from this course, and the prof. was amazing. 

I also enjoyed writing for the screen - so if you have any desire to explore writing scripts, I recommend this class

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There was a fee I had to pay on maybe 2000 Dkk - I'm not completely sure what it was for - but some of it was for a public transfer card, that was mandatory for some reason. maybe also some health insurance was covered in the fee?

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries was expensive - but slowly you find out where to buy different things. Denmark is also expensive, so I don't think it was that big of a chok, that it might have been for people from other places in the world.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Regarding sports and outdoors activity, there was a lot! But other than that, not so much.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't look into it that much - but I heard from other exchange students that there were many outdoors trips and clubs to join. I'm more interested in art, films and music, and that was definitely not something that was easy to get access to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard good things about the outdoorsclubs. And also just in general to explore the nature in Canada.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes, go skiing or maybe visit Seattle in USA.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, the area is a University district, and Canadians are friendly. Although downtown can be a bit overwhelming, because of some pretty rough areas.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As a bit of an introvert, it could be challenging that people are very chatty.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most people will help you if you ask.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get to know the grading system - I got pretty stressed out because I thought I had to do more than was actually needed. 
Ask for help - your prof. are really interested in helping you out. 
Don't stress too much in the beginning, there's a lot to take in, and if you don't feel like going skiing or hiking in the first couple of weekends, there is plenty of time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: More activity is required than at KU, so try not to be too perfectionistic about assignments and midterms etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a different country and trying a different university

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to a different learning style and different expectations.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
